target_customer: Notaries, title and mortgage firms, law firms and businesses that sign agreements remotely
problem: Transactions that needed an in-person signing could not be done remotely with trust and identity verification.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription and per-transaction fees for eSignature and remote online notarization

founders.name: Moktar Yusuf
founders.background_notes: Prior experience not stated on sources seen.

competitors.name: Notarize
competitors.traction_then: Partnered with Snapdocs for digital closings in September 2021

competitors.name: Secured Signing
competitors.traction_then: Added video confirmation to eSignatures in 2017

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining live video, synchronized document editing, identity verification and notarization compliance is standard engineering with compliance work.

defensibility.rationale: Video plus signing was copyable, though state notary approvals and integrations with title workflows added some friction.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well funded notarization and eSignature players existed; Pactima was ultimately acquired by Snapdocs in 2026 and became Snapdocs RON.

market_need_then: The remote-work shift of 2020 and 2021 and temporary RON rules created demand for transactions previously done in person.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, trust focused, tagline Leading edge eSigning, made simple

rebrands.why: Acquired by Snapdocs and integrated into its platform

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community evidence about the brand; it was retired after acquisition.

outcome_analysis: Pactima rode the remote transaction boom, raised an oversubscribed seed led by FundersClub in 2021 and built a broader eNotary and eSignature suite with compliance credentials. It was acquired by Snapdocs, announced in a founders letter dated September 1, 2026, and the product became Snapdocs RON. The price and exact round sizes are not public, so the quality of the outcome is uncertain.
notes: CB Insights lists total funding of only $130K, which conflicts with the multimillion-dollar seed headline from OBJ; the CB Insights figure is unverified and not recorded. No second outlet found for the seed amount. Acquisition source is the company's own announcement plus Snapdocs support pages, no independent coverage seen. Competitor sources are partly 2017 and 2021 and do not describe traction in detail.
